lines.cap: **Narrator:** This is Kavya. She is twelve. Monday morning, Room 2-14: the Media Club studio. Also the mop cupboard.
**Mr Tan:** Kavya. Big story for **8B News**. The canteen gets **one** new stall: **bubble tea** or **ice kachang**.
**Mr Tan:** The principal decides on Friday. Her exact words: "**Show me the data.**"
**Kavya:** So we survey the school and report the result. **Fairly.**
**Priya:** Done! I already asked. **100%** want bubble tea!
**Kavya:** Priya. **Who** did you ask?
**Priya:** My bubble tea group chat. All **43** of us.
**Narrator:** But this documentary is about the old computer in the corner. Inside it: the **Fact-Check Desk**.
**Inspector Axis:** Inspector **Axis**. Fact-checker. I've seen a thousand graphs, kid. Most of them were lying.
**Inspector Axis:** Asking your own fan club is a **biased sample**. Bubble tea fans say bubble tea. Shocking.
**Priya:** It's not biased. It's **loyal**.
**Inspector Axis:** Five days. One canteen. **1200** pupils. And somebody has to **check the axes**.
**Narrator:** Show Me the Data. Episode 18: The Great Canteen Vote.
**Inspector Axis:** Every case goes round the **enquiry cycle**. **Plan. Collect. Process and represent. Interpret.** Then round again.
**Dad:** Simple. Ask **all 1200** pupils.
**Inspector Axis:** Asking everyone is a **census**. Too slow. Ask a **sample**: a smaller group that's **representative**.
**Ah Boy:** I'll stand outside the bubble tea shop and ask **1000** people!
**Inspector Axis:** A **convenience** sample. Big, easy, and **biased**: you'd only meet bubble tea fans. **How** you choose beats **how many**.
**Kavya:** **Simple random**: a computer picks. Or **systematic**: 1200 ÷ 60 = **20**, so every **20th** name from a random start.
**Ah Boy:** Random start: **7**! Then 27, 47, 67...
**Kavya:** The 60th name is 7 + 59 × 20 = **1187**. Still on the list.
**Mum:** Or **stratified**: each year group in proportion. Sec 1's **320** pupils: 320 ÷ 20 = **16**.
**Mum:** My question! "How much do you spend on drinks?" **$0–$2**, **$2–$4**, **$5 or more**.
**Inspector Axis:** Three problems. No **time frame**. An **overlap** at $2. And a **gap**: where does **$4.50** go?
**Kavya:** Fixed: "In the **last 5 school days**..." Under $5, $5 to $9.99, $10 or more.
**Kavya:** **Name it**: categorical, like favourite stall. **Count it**: discrete, like cups a week. **Measure it**: continuous, like queue time.
**Ah Boy:** My shoe size is continuous! My feet keep growing!
**Mum:** Your **feet** are continuous. **Shoe sizes** jump: 2, 2½, 3. **Discrete.** And you need new shoes.
**Priya:** Before you vote: **don't you agree** bubble tea is the best?
**Inspector Axis:** A **leading question**. It pushes people towards one answer.
**Tally:** Tally! I count! One, two, three, four... **GATE!** The fifth stroke goes across. Count in **fives**!
**Kavya:** Bubble tea **26**, ice kachang **22**, don't mind **12**. Total **60**: the frequencies add up to the sample.
**Auntie Rose:** Kavya! Auntie timed her trial queue! **16** waits in seconds. Put them in **groups of ten**!
**Tally:** Forty seconds! Where does **40** go?! PANIC!
**Mr Tan:** **40 ≤ t < 50**: at least forty, but **less than** fifty. Forty goes in. Fifty goes next door.
**Kavya:** Frequencies **2, 4, 6, 3, 1**. Total **16**. The **modal class** is 40 ≤ t < 50: the most common.
**Mr Tan:** Now a **two-way table**. Every row and column adds to its total. Find a line with **one gap**, and **subtract**.
**Kavya:** Lower secondary, ice kachang: 31 − 17 − 5 = **9**.
**Priya:** Upper secondary, bubble tea: 26 − 17 = **9**. Ice kachang: 22 − 9 = **13**.
**Priya:** So the big kids prefer ice kachang. The big kids have **no taste**.
**Dame Pie:** **Dame Pie**. Pie chart. My great-great-grandmother was **Florence Nightingale's** rose diagram, darling.
**Kavya:** Sixty pupils share **360°**. So **one** pupil gets 360 ÷ 60 = **6°**.
**Dame Pie:** **One first, then multiply.** Bubble tea: 26 × 6 = **156°**. Ice kachang: 22 × 6 = **132°**. Don't mind: 12 × 6 = **72°**. Total **360°**.
**Auntie Rose:** Kavya! Auntie's pie from the hawker centre: ice kachang is **90°**, out of **200** customers!
**Kavya:** Backwards: 90 ÷ 360 × 200 = **50** customers.
**Priya:** Our ice kachang slice is **132°**. Hers is only **90°**. So **more** people like ours!
**Dame Pie:** Never compare two pies without their **totals**, darling. 132° of 60 is **22** people. 90° of 200 is **50**.
**Kavya:** Lower and upper secondary **side by side**: a **dual bar chart**. Best for comparing the groups.
**Mr Tan:** **Stack** the parts instead, and each bar's height shows the **total**: a **compound bar chart**.
**Dame Pie:** And now... the **weather**! Auntie's ice kachang sales, every three months for two years.
**Kavya:** A **time-series graph**: time along the bottom. **Seasonal pattern**: it peaks every **April to June**, the hottest months.
**Mr Tan:** For the **trend**, compare the **same** quarter each year. Year 2 beats Year 1 **every** time. **Upwards.**
**Priya:** Great show, Dame Pie. Can I have a **slice**?
**Dame Pie:** **How dare you.**
**Priya:** Trial day! Bubble tea serving times, in seconds: 34, 27, 45, 31... **fifteen** of them! What's the **middle** one?
**Stemmy:** Stemmy! **Stem-and-leaf**! The **tens** digit is the **stem**. The **units** digit is the **leaf**.
**Stemmy:** 34: stem 3, leaf 4. **One digit** per leaf. Then the leaves go **in order**, smallest by the stem.
**Stemmy:** And a **key**: 3 | 4 means **34 seconds**. Now... where did I put my key?
**Stemmy:** Without my key I could be **34**, **3.4** or **340**! Who AM I?!
**Kavya:** **15** leaves, so the median is the (15 + 1) ÷ 2 = **8th** value. Count along: **34 seconds**.
**Stemmy:** Mode **31 s**: the only repeat. Range: 48 − 22 = **26 s**.
**Auntie Rose:** Auntie's times also! **11** bowls. Put me on the same stems!
**Stemmy:** **Back-to-back!** Auntie's leaves go on the **left**, reading **outwards**. Her median: **28 s**. Her range: 44 − 21 = **23 s**.
**Mr Tan:** Lower median: Auntie is generally **faster**. Smaller range: more **consistent**.
**Stemmy:** Found my key! I'm **34** again. What a relief.
**Mr Tan:** Thursday. Staff room survey. Of **30** teachers, **18** like bubble tea and **12** like ice kachang.
**Priya:** 18 + 12 = **30**. Every single teacher likes one!
**Vera:** Hi! **Vera**, the bubble tea circle. My sister **Nina**, ice kachang. The **Venn diagram** twins. We **share the middle**.
**Mr Tan:** **5** teachers like **both**.
**Nina:** **Middle first**, then outwards! The **overlap** means **both**. Five go in here.
**Vera:** Bubble tea **only**: 18 − 5 = **13**.
**Nina:** Ice kachang **only**: 12 − 5 = **7**.
**Kavya:** Inside the circles: 13 + 5 + 7 = **25**. So **neither**: 30 − 25 = **5**.
**Vera:** Priya, you counted the **both** teachers **twice**. 18 + 12 − 5 = **25**.
**Priya:** So five teachers like **neither**?
**Mr Tan:** Five teachers like **kopi**.
**Ah Boy:** My homework! Sort **1 to 20**: multiple of 3? Even?
**Dad:** A **Carroll diagram**: a **yes or no** grid for each question. Named after **Lewis Carroll**, of Alice in Wonderland.
**Vera:** Same **four groups** as a Venn diagram: 3 + 3 + 7 + 7 = **20**.
**Auntie Rose:** Thursday night, Auntie's stall. Every day Auntie writes the **temperature**, and how many **bowls** I sell.
**Kavya:** Two numbers for each day. Plot every day as a point: a **scatter graph**.
**Ah Boy:** The dots are walking **uphill**!
**Lofty:** Lofty. **Line of best fit**. Uphill is **positive**. Downhill is **negative**, dude.
**Kavya:** **Positive correlation**: as the temperature **increases**, sales **tend to increase**.
**Dad:** Easy. Just **join the dots**.
**Lofty:** No **dot-to-dot**, and no need to hit the **origin**. One straight line through the **middle**: as many points above as below.
**Lofty:** I pass through (26, 12) and (34, 108). That's **96** bowls over **8** degrees: **12** bowls per degree.
**Auntie Rose:** Tomorrow's forecast: **33 °C**. How many bowls must Auntie prepare?
**Kavya:** That's 7 degrees above 26 °C: 12 + 7 × 12 = **96 bowls**.
**Lofty:** 33 is **inside** the data: **interpolation**. Fairly reliable.
**Kavya:** And **45 °C**? That's **extrapolation**: way outside the data. Risky. At 45 °C, **we'd** be the ice kachang.
**Dad:** Hot soup on hot days: **negative correlation**. Ah Boy's shoe size and spelling marks: **no correlation**.
**Priya:** Kavya! Ice kachang sales and **sunburn** both go up together! Ice kachang **causes sunburn**! Ban ice kachang!
**Inspector Axis:** **Correlation is not causation.** A **third variable**, the hot sun, drives both.
**Narrator:** Friday. 8B News goes out live to the whole school.
**Priya:** My poster! Bubble tea sold **102**, ice kachang **98**. Look how much **taller** we are!
**Inspector Axis:** **Check. The. Axes.** This one starts at **95**.
**Inspector Axis:** So the bars are **7** and **3** tall: yours looks **twice** as big. Really? About **4%** more.
**Kavya:** Bars must start at **0**. Then they look almost **equal**, because they **are**.
**Priya:** Fine. Poster two. We got **twice** as many likes online, so our cup is **twice as tall** and **twice as wide**!
**Inspector Axis:** 2 × 2 = **4**. Four times the **area**. It looks like **four times** as many.
**Kavya:** Choosing charts, live: votes per stall, a **bar** or **pie chart**. Sales over time, a **line graph**. Temperature and bowls, a **scatter graph**.
**Priya:** And the queue times! A bar chart with nice **gaps**!
**Inspector Axis:** Time is **continuous**. The classes meet, so the bars **touch**. That's a **frequency diagram**.
**Kavya:** Stretch: plot each class **midpoint**, like (20 + 30) ÷ 2 = **25**, against its frequency.
**Inspector Axis:** Join them up: a **frequency polygon**. Bubble tea's polygon sits further **right**: **longer** waits.
**Mr Tan:** And the principal's decision, based on the data...
**Auntie Rose:** Auntie Rose sells **ice kachang**... **with bubble tea pearls**! Everybody happy!
**Vera:** It's **both**! The **overlap**!

chapters.title: The Fact-Check Desk saves you some marks

lines.cap: **Narrator:** Before the credits: six ways to save marks.
**Stemmy:** One. Every stem-and-leaf needs a **key**, and leaves **in order**, **one digit** each. Never 3 | 12.
**Auntie Rose:** Two. A **boundary value**: 40 seconds goes in **40 ≤ t < 50**, not the class before.
**Dame Pie:** Three. Angles add up to **360°**. Frequencies add up to the **total**. **Check**, darling.
**Lofty:** Four. Correlation **in context**: "as temperature increases, sales tend to increase".
**Inspector Axis:** Five. **Continuous** data: the bars **touch**. No gaps.
**Priya:** Six. Calling a sample **biased**? Say **who** is left out, and why. Mine left out everyone outside my group chat.
**Narrator:** Show Me the Data will return.
**Narrator:** Monday. Kavya's flat.
**Ah Boy:** I did a survey! "Who is the best child in this family?" **100%** said **me**!
**Kavya:** Ah Boy. **Who** did you ask?
**Ah Boy:** **Me.**
**Inspector Axis:** Sample size: **one**. **Biased.** Case closed.
